proposals.before: As to all who resell private salt for consumption: fifty-seven strokes of the bamboo; the confiscation statute does not apply.
proposals.after: As to all who purchase private salt for consumption: fifty-seven strokes of the bamboo; the confiscation statute does not apply.
proposals.reason: 轉買 here means buying illicit salt (for eating), not reselling it; the idiomatic already correctly has buy.

proposals.before: Brothers who in a quarrel jointly beat their fathers to death are all executed.
proposals.after: Brothers who in a quarrel jointly beat their paternal uncles to death are all executed.
proposals.reason: In this kinship-homicide statute, 諸父 means paternal uncles, matching nearby 伯叔母 and 從父, not fathers.

proposals.before: As to all brothers who in a quarrel jointly plot to beat to death their fathers: all are executed.
proposals.after: As to all brothers who in a quarrel jointly plot to beat to death their paternal uncles: all are executed.
proposals.reason: 諸父 in this legal context denotes paternal uncles, not fathers.

proposals.before: If a man kills his wife's husband through adultery without the adulteress's knowledge, the penalty is reduced from death.
proposals.after: If through adultery a man kills the woman's lawful husband without the adulteress's knowledge, the penalty is reduced from death.
proposals.reason: 本夫 is the adulteress's lawful husband; 'his wife's husband' is nonsensical and misidentifies the victim.

proposals.before: As to all who through adultery kill their own husband while the adulteress did not know: sentence with death reduced.
proposals.after: As to all who through adultery kill her lawful husband while the adulteress did not know: sentence with death reduced.
proposals.reason: Silent subject is the adulterer killing 本夫 (her lawful husband), not someone killing their own husband.

proposals.before: Those who demand adultery and, when refused, beat their wife to death are sentenced as armed robbers who kill.
proposals.after: Those who demand adultery and, when refused, beat the woman to death are sentenced as armed robbers who kill.
proposals.reason: 其婦 is the woman who refused the illicit advance, not necessarily the offender's wife.

proposals.before: As to all who seek adultery and, when refused, beat their wife to death: sentenced as for an armed robber who kills.
proposals.after: As to all who seek adultery and, when refused, beat the woman to death: sentenced as for an armed robber who kills.
proposals.reason: 其婦 refers to the woman from whom adultery was sought, not specifically a wife.

proposals.before: up to twenty guan, the ringleader is executed and the rest exiled afar.
proposals.after: when the loot reaches twenty guan, the ringleader is executed and the rest exiled afar.
proposals.reason: 至二十貫 marks the threshold at which the death penalty applies, not an upper bound of 'up to'.

proposals.before: up to twenty guan: seventy-seven strokes.
proposals.after: when the loot reaches twenty guan: seventy-seven strokes.
proposals.reason: 至二十貫 is the threshold amount for this penalty step, not 'up to twenty guan'.

proposals.before: Sons, younger brothers, or sons-in-law who steal and surrender a father's, elder brother's, or father-in-law's head are exempt as if they had surrendered voluntarily.
proposals.after: When a son steals and his father reports him, when a younger brother steals and his elder brother reports him, or when a son-in-law steals and his father-in-law reports him, all are exempt as if they had surrendered voluntarily.
proposals.reason: Chinese 首 here means report/denounce a thief (出首), not 'head'; the clause concerns close kin reporting a relative's theft, treated like voluntary surrender.

proposals.before: As to all sons who steal and surrender their fathers' heads, younger brothers who steal and surrender elder brothers' heads, and sons-in-law who steal and surrender fathers-in-law's heads: all are exempt like voluntary surrenderants.
proposals.after: As to all cases where a son steals and the father reports him, a younger brother steals and the elder brother reports him, or a son-in-law steals and the father-in-law reports him: all are exempt like voluntary surrenderants.
proposals.reason: Literal English mistranslates 首 as 'heads'; in this statute 父首/兄首/翁首 means the senior relative reports the thief.

proposals.before: Slaves who steal and surrender their master's head are sentenced without tattoo or double restitution and remain their master's slaves.
proposals.after: When a slave steals and the master reports him, the slave is sentenced without tattoo or double restitution and remains the master's slave.
proposals.reason: Parallel to s0416: 主首 means the master reports the slave's theft, not surrendering a severed head.

proposals.before: As to all slaves who steal and surrender their master's head: sentenced, exempt from tattoo, no double restitution, still returned to the master as slaves.
proposals.after: As to all slaves who steal and whose master reports them: sentenced, exempt from tattoo, no double restitution, still returned to the master as slaves.
proposals.reason: Literal English mistranslates 首 as 'head'; the legal sense is the master's reporting (出首) of the slave thief.

decisions.reason: s0017 轉買私鹽食用者 means buyers of illicit salt for eating; 轉買 is purchase, not resale, and the idiomatic already has buy.
In this kinship-homicide cluster, 諸父 are paternal uncles, aligning with nearby 伯叔母 and 從父; 'fathers' misreads the victim class.
Same statute: 諸父 denotes paternal uncles, not fathers; the literal must match that kinship sense.
本夫 is the adulteress's lawful husband; 'his wife's husband' invents a nonsensical victim and misidentifies 本夫.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 諸因奸殺其本夫，奸婦不知情

decisions.reason: The silent agent is the adulterer killing 本夫; 'their own husband' wrongly makes the victim the killer's husband.
求奸不從…毆死其婦 refers to beating the woman who refused the advance; 其婦 is not the offender's wife.
Same clause: 其婦 is the woman sought for illicit sex, so 'wife' over-specifies and misleads.
至二十貫 is the threshold at which the ringleader dies after the prior 'any loot' step; 'up to' reverses the scale.
In the graded theft scale after 十貫以下, 至二十貫 marks the next threshold, not an upper bound.
父首/兄首/翁首 means the senior relative reports (出首) the thief; 首 is not 'head', and nearby 不首/自首 confirm the reporting sense.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 諸子盜父首、弟盜兄首、婿盜翁首，並同自首者免罪

decisions.reason: Literal 'surrender … heads' mistranslates 首; the statute treats senior kin reporting the junior thief like voluntary surrender.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 子盜父首、弟盜兄首、婿盜翁首

decisions.reason: Parallel to s0416: 奴盜主首 is a slave's theft reported by the master, not surrender of a severed head.
Same 首 = report reading: the master reports the slave thief; 'master's head' is unsupported.
